import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Dataset provided as a string
data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Create a descriptive label for 'has_video_4k' for better legend readability
df['has_video_4k_label'] = df['has_video_4k'].map({0: 'No 4K Video', 1: 'Has 4K Video'})

# Set up the matplotlib figure
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize relationships between key camera attributes
# X-axis: Megapixels
# Y-axis: Price
# Color: Body Type
# Style (marker): Has 4K Video capability
# Size: Weight in grams
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='body_type',
    style='has_video_4k_label',
    size='weight_grams',
    sizes=(100, 1000),  # Adjust marker size range for better distinction
    palette='viridis',
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=0.5,
    alpha=0.9
)

# Add titles and labels for clarity
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Body Type, 4K Video, and Weight', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement and appearance
plt.legend(title='Camera Attributes', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0, frameon=True)

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Ensure all elements fit within the figure area
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png')

# Close the plot to free up memory
plt.close()
